facts.fact: The Controller and Auditor General's information systems audit for the year to 30 June 2025 treats Local Government Authorities as users of centrally hosted government systems: it lists 59 LGAs that made TZS 9.90 billion of procurement outside the national e-procurement system NeST, which they are required to use, and names district, town, municipal and city councils among 34 entities whose asset records in the Ministry of Finance's GAMIS did not match their registers; it does not describe the councils' offices or how they are connected.

The Controller and Auditor General states that PMO-RALG hosts and manages the TAUSI revenue system, FFARS and GoTHOMIS as centralised systems that user public entities rely on, audited for the period 1 July 2024 to 30 June 2025; the audit does not say how many councils work in them or how their offices are connected.

systems.tiers: centrally hosted and managed by PMO-RALG for user entities; local government revenue

systems.system: Facility Financial Accounting and Reporting System (FFARS)
systems.tiers: centrally hosted and managed by PMO-RALG; access for departed staff not revoked in time (2024/25)

systems.system: Government of Tanzania Health Operations Management Information System (GoTHOMIS)
systems.tiers: primary health facilities and district hospitals; a 2016 directive requires all LGAs to install it in health facilities; 23 LGAs collected TZS 6.65 billion outside it in 2024/25, from collection reports of standalone installations, up from 12 LGAs the year before
all procuring entities, LGAs included; 59 LGAs procured TZS 9.90 billion outside it in 2024/25, against 88 entities and TZS 31.81 billion in 2023/24
all accounting officers; 34 entities, mostly district, town, municipal and city councils and two regional secretariats, used it ineffectively in 2024/25 (41 in 2023/24)
mandatory accounting system for public entities; the 80 entities found outside it are public authorities and other bodies, none an LGA
all government entities, payroll and human resources; no LGA finding stated
government-wide payments; no local government tier stated

systems.owner: Tanzania Rural and Urban Roads Agency (TARURA)
systems.tiers: upgrade planned for November 2022 to April 2023, still in planning in September 2025

note: No statement on council offices' connection, its provider or the number of councils connected; the two facts record only that councils work in centrally hosted systems. No LGA appears among the 133 entities rated for ICT compliance.
